title: Culpable homicide
old_text: Whoever causes death by doing an act with the intention of causing death, or with the intention of causing such bodily injury as is likely to cause death, or with the knowledge that he is likely by such act to cause death, commits the offence of culpable homicide.
new_text: Whoever causes death by doing an act with the intention of causing death, or with the intention of causing such bodily injury as is likely to cause death, or with the knowledge that he is likely by such act to cause death, commits the offence of culpable homicide.
punishment_old: Substantive definition; punishment prescribed under IPC Section 304.
punishment_new: Substantive definition; punishment prescribed under BNS Section 105.
explanation: Defines the genus offence of culpable homicide across its three classic mental states: intention to cause death, intention to inflict fatal bodily injury, or knowledge of probable death. The definitions, explanations, and illustrations remain identical to IPC Section 299.

title: Murder
old_text: Culpable homicide is murder if the act by which the death is caused is done with the intention of causing death; or with the intention of causing bodily injury known to be likely to cause death; or sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death; or with knowledge of imminently dangerous act without excuse, subject to five specific exceptions.
new_text: Culpable homicide is murder if the act by which death is caused is done with the intention of causing death; or with intention of causing such bodily injury as the offender knows to be likely to cause death; or bodily injury sufficient in ordinary course of nature; or imminently dangerous act with knowledge of fatal probability, subject to five exceptions (grave & sudden provocation, private defence, public servant acting in good faith, sudden fight, and consent of adult over 18).
punishment_old: Substantive definition; punishment prescribed under IPC Section 302.
punishment_new: Substantive definition; punishment prescribed under BNS Section 103.
explanation: Defines the species offence of murder and preserves the five statutory exceptions where homicide does not amount to murder. Renumbered from IPC Section 300 with simplified structural phrasing.

title: Culpable homicide by causing death of person other than person whose death was intended
old_text: If a person, by doing anything which he intends or knows to be likely to cause death, commits culpable homicide by causing the death of any person, whose death he neither intends nor knows himself to be likely to cause, the culpable homicide is of the description of which it would have been if he had caused the death of the person whose death was intended.
new_text: If a person, by doing anything which he intends or knows to be likely to cause death, commits culpable homicide by causing the death of any person, whose death he neither intends nor knows himself to be likely to cause, the culpable homicide is of the description of which it would have been if he had caused the death of the person whose death he intended or knew himself likely to cause.
punishment_old: Punished as murder or culpable homicide as if the intended target had died.
punishment_new: Punished as murder or culpable homicide as if the intended target had died.
explanation: Codifies the doctrine of transferred malice (aberratio ictus), ensuring an offender cannot escape murder charges because their bullet or weapon struck an unintended bystander. Renumbered from IPC Section 301.

title: Punishment for murder
old_text: Whoever commits murder shall be punished with death, or imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine (single general provision under IPC 302).
new_text: Sub-section (1): Whoever commits murder shall be punished with death or imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine. Sub-section (2): When a group of five or more persons acting in concert commits murder on the ground of race, caste or community, sex, place of birth, language, personal belief or any other ground, each member of such group shall be punished with death or with imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.
punishment_old: Death or imprisonment for life, and fine (IPC Section 302).
punishment_new: Death or imprisonment for life, and fine (BNS Section 103(1)); Mob Lynching by group of 5+ on discriminatory grounds punishable with death or life imprisonment, and fine (BNS Section 103(2)).
explanation: A historic development: while sub-section (1) preserves the general sentencing for murder, sub-section (2) introduces a landmark statutory provision specifically penalizing mob lynching and group murders committed on grounds of caste, community, race, sex, or belief with mandatory capital punishment or life imprisonment for every participating member.

title: Punishment for murder by life-convict
old_text: Whoever, being under sentence of imprisonment for life, commits murder, shall be punished with death (IPC Section 303 struck down as unconstitutional by Supreme Court in Mithu v. State of Punjab, 1983).
new_text: Whoever, being under sentence of imprisonment for life, commits murder, shall be punished with death or with imprisonment for life, which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person's natural life, and shall also be liable to fine.
punishment_old: Mandatory death sentence (void and unenforceable under Mithu v. State of Punjab).
punishment_new: Death or imprisonment for the remainder of natural life, and fine.
explanation: Cures the constitutional invalidity of former IPC Section 303 by removing the mandatory death penalty struck down in Mithu v. State of Punjab, providing judicial discretion between capital punishment and imprisonment for the remainder of natural life.

title: Punishment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder
old_text: Whoever commits culpable homicide not amounting to murder shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to 10 years and fine (if act done with intention); or imprisonment up to 10 years, or fine, or both (if act done with knowledge).
new_text: Whoever commits culpable homicide not amounting to murder shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than five years but which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine (if act done with intention); or with imprisonment up to ten years, or with fine, or with both (if act done with knowledge).
punishment_old: Part I (intent): Life imprisonment or up to 10 years, and fine; Part II (knowledge): Imprisonment up to 10 years, or fine, or both.
punishment_new: Part I (intent): Life imprisonment or imprisonment 5 to 10 years, and fine; Part II (knowledge): Imprisonment up to 10 years, or fine, or both.
explanation: Preserves the two-part sentencing bifurcation between intentional culpable homicide and knowledge-based homicide, while introducing a minimum floor of 5 years imprisonment for intentional culpable homicide not amounting to murder. Renumbered from IPC Section 304.

title: Causing death by negligence
old_text: Whoever causes the death of any person by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both (IPC Section 304A).
new_text: Sub-section (1): Whoever causes death of any person by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide, shall be punished with imprisonment up to five years, and with fine; and if such act is done by a registered medical practitioner while performing medical procedure, with imprisonment up to two years and fine. Sub-section (2): Whoever causes death by rash and negligent driving and escapes without reporting to police or magistrate soon after incident, shall be punished with imprisonment up to ten years, and fine.
punishment_old: Imprisonment of either description up to 2 years, or fine, or both (IPC 304A).
punishment_new: General negligence: up to 5 years and fine; Medical practitioner: up to 2 years and fine (106(1)); Hit-and-run driving: up to 10 years and fine (106(2)).
explanation: Significantly enhances penalties for criminal negligence from 2 years to 5 years, creates an explicit statutory carve-out for registered medical practitioners performing procedures (capped at 2 years), and introduces a stringent 10-year penalty for hit-and-run drivers who flee without reporting.

title: Abetment of suicide of child or person of unsound mind
old_text: If any person under eighteen years of age, any insane person, any delirious person, any idiot, or any person in a state of intoxication, commits suicide, whoever abets the commission of such suicide, shall be punished with death or imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine.
new_text: If any child or any person of unsound mind, or any person in a state of intoxication, commits suicide, whoever abets the commission of such suicide, shall be punished with death or imprisonment for life, or imprisonment for a term which may extend to fourteen years, and shall also be liable to fine.
punishment_old: Death, or imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine.
punishment_new: Death, or imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to 14 years, and fine.
explanation: Penalizes abetment of suicide of vulnerable individuals (children, mentally unsound or intoxicated persons), raising the maximum term of determinate imprisonment from 10 to 14 years. Renumbered from IPC Section 305.

title: Abetment of suicide
old_text: If any person commits suicide, whoever abets the commission of such suicide, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
new_text: If any person commits suicide, whoever abets the commission of such suicide, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
punishment_old: Imprisonment of either description up to 10 years, and fine.
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to 10 years, and fine.
explanation: Governs the general offence of abetment of suicide, requiring clear active instigation or intentional facilitation. Renumbered from IPC Section 306.

title: Attempt to murder
old_text: Whoever does any act with such intention or knowledge, and under such circumstances that, if he by that act caused death, he would be guilty of murder, shall be punished with imprisonment up to 10 years and fine; if hurt caused, life imprisonment or up to 10 years; life-convicts causing hurt could be punished with death.
new_text: Sub-section (1): Whoever does any act with such intention or knowledge that if death were caused he would be guilty of murder, shall be punished with imprisonment up to ten years and fine; and if hurt is caused, with imprisonment for life or up to ten years and fine. Sub-section (2): When any person offending under sub-section (1) is under sentence of imprisonment for life and causes hurt, he may be punished with death or imprisonment for life (remainder of natural life).
punishment_old: Up to 10 years and fine; if hurt caused, life or up to 10 years; life-convict causing hurt: death.
punishment_new: Up to 10 years and fine; if hurt caused, life or up to 10 years and fine; life-convict causing hurt: death or imprisonment for remainder of natural life.
explanation: Penalizes attempts to commit murder with graduated penalties depending on whether physical hurt resulted. Sub-section (2) removes the mandatory capital sentence for life-convicts, adding natural life imprisonment as a constitutional alternative. Renumbered from IPC Section 307.

title: Attempt to commit culpable homicide
old_text: Whoever does any act with such intention or knowledge, and under such circumstances that, if he by that act caused death, he would be guilty of culpable homicide not amounting to murder, shall be punished with imprisonment up to 3 years or fine or both; if hurt caused, up to 7 years or fine or both.
new_text: Whoever does any act with such intention or knowledge, and under such circumstances that, if he by that act caused death, he would be guilty of culpable homicide not amounting to murder, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both; and if hurt is caused, with imprisonment up to seven years, or with fine, or with both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both; if hurt is caused, imprisonment up to 7 years, or fine, or both.
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both; if hurt is caused, imprisonment up to 7 years, or fine, or both.
explanation: Penalizes failed or intercepted acts which, had death occurred, would have constituted culpable homicide not amounting to murder. Renumbered from IPC Section 308.

title: Organised crime
old_text: None (Organised crime was previously prosecuted under state-specific special enactments such as MCOCA, UP-PCOCA, or under ordinary IPC conspiracy and gang sections).
new_text: Any continuing unlawful activity including kidnapping, robbery, vehicle theft, extortion, land grabbing, contract killing, economic offence, cybercrimes, trafficking, or illegal goods/services committed by a person singly or jointly as a member of an organized crime syndicate by violence, intimidation or coercion to gain direct or indirect material benefit. If death results: death or imprisonment for life and fine not less than ₹10 lakhs; in other cases: imprisonment not less than 5 years up to life and fine not less than ₹5 lakhs.
punishment_old: Not codified in the general Indian Penal Code.
punishment_new: If death results: death or imprisonment for life and fine not less than ₹10,00,000; in other cases: rigorous imprisonment 5 years to life and fine not less than ₹5,00,000.
explanation: A major statutory addition codifying organized crime syndicates, mafia networks, contract killing, and illicit extortion rings directly into India's substantive general criminal code. Prescribes mandatory heavy fines and capital punishment / life imprisonment where death ensues.

title: Petty organised crime
old_text: None (Street-level syndicate crimes were booked under individual theft, cheating or hurt sections of IPC).
new_text: Whoever, being a member of a group or gang, singly or jointly, commits any act of theft, snatching, cheating, unauthorized selling of tickets, betting, gambling, or illicit public examination paper leaking by deception or trickery, commits petty organised crime. Punished with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than one year but which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
punishment_old: Charged as simple theft, cheating, or gambling under dispersed IPC sections.
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description not less than 1 year but which may extend to 7 years, and fine.
explanation: Introduces a new specialized penal offence targeting recurring gang-operated street crime, pickpocketing, snatching, illegal ticketing networks, and examination paper leaks. Imposes a mandatory minimum sentence of one year.

title: Terrorist act
old_text: None (Terrorism was exclusively prosecuted under special legislation, notably the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967).
new_text: Whoever does any act with intent to threaten or likely to threaten the unity, integrity, sovereignty, or security of India, or to strike terror in people by using bombs, dynamite, firearms, lethal weapons, poisonous gases, or cyber means. If death of any person results: death or imprisonment for life, and fine; in other cases: imprisonment not less than 5 years up to life, and fine. Harbouring, membership, and proceeds of terrorism are equally penalized.
punishment_old: Not codified in IPC (prosecuted under UAPA, 1967).
punishment_new: If death results: death or imprisonment for life, and fine; other cases: imprisonment not less than 5 years up to life, and fine.
explanation: Codifies terrorism directly into the general penal code for the first time in Indian legal history, defining acts that threaten India's unity, sovereignty, or public terror. Operates concurrently with special anti-terror enactments like UAPA.

title: Hurt
old_text: Whoever causes bodily pain, disease or infirmity to any person is said to cause hurt.
new_text: Whoever causes bodily pain, disease or infirmity to any person is said to cause hurt.
punishment_old: Substantive definition; punishment prescribed under IPC Section 323.
punishment_new: Substantive definition; punishment prescribed under BNS Section 115.
explanation: Defines basic hurt through the three statutory components: bodily pain, disease, or infirmity. Identical in wording to IPC Section 319.

title: Voluntarily causing hurt
old_text: IPC Section 321 defined voluntarily causing hurt; IPC Section 323 provided punishment of imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine up to ₹1,000, or both.
new_text: Sub-section (1) defines voluntarily causing hurt (doing any act with intention or knowledge of causing hurt); Sub-section (2) prescribes punishment with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees, or with both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine up to ₹1,000, or both (IPC 323).
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine up to ₹10,000, or both (BNS 115(2)).
explanation: Merges the definition (IPC 321) and penal clause (IPC 323) into one section while increasing the maximum fine tenfold from ₹1,000 to ₹10,000.

title: Grievous hurt
old_text: Designated eight specific kinds of hurt as grievous: emasculation, permanent privation of sight of either eye, permanent privation of hearing of either ear, privation of any member or joint, destruction/impairment of powers of any member or joint, permanent disfiguration of head or face, fracture or dislocation of bone or tooth, and hurt endangering life or causing severe bodily pain or inability to follow ordinary pursuits for 20 days.
new_text: Enumerates eight designated kinds of hurt as grievous: emasculation; permanent privation of sight of either eye; permanent privation of hearing of either ear; privation of any member or joint; destruction or permanent impairing of powers of any member or joint; permanent disfiguration of head or face; fracture or dislocation of bone or tooth; and any hurt which endangers life or causes severe bodily pain or prevents following ordinary pursuits for fifteen days.
punishment_old: Substantive definition; punishment prescribed under IPC Section 325.
punishment_new: Substantive definition; punishment prescribed under BNS Section 117.
explanation: Retains the eight categories of grievous hurt with one vital modification: in the eighth clause, the duration of severe pain or inability to follow ordinary pursuits is reduced from 20 days to 15 days, broadening victim protection.

title: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt
old_text: IPC Section 322 defined voluntarily causing grievous hurt; IPC Section 325 prescribed punishment of imprisonment up to 7 years and fine.
new_text: Sub-section (1) defines voluntarily causing grievous hurt; Sub-section (2) provides punishment with imprisonment up to seven years and fine; Sub-section (3) provides that whoever causes grievous hurt which results in permanent disability or persistent vegetative state shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment not less than ten years up to life, and fine; Sub-section (4) punishes grievous hurt caused by a group of five or more on grounds of caste/community with imprisonment up to seven years and fine.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 7 years and fine (IPC Section 325).
punishment_new: General: up to 7 years and fine (117(2)); Permanent disability / vegetative state: rigorous imprisonment 10 years to life, and fine (117(3)); Group of 5+ on grounds of race/caste: imprisonment up to 7 years and fine (117(4)).
explanation: Merges definition and general sentencing while creating two brand-new aggravated sub-clauses: Section 117(3) introduces 10-year to life sentences for causing permanent disability or vegetative state, and Section 117(4) penalizes mob attacks causing grievous hurt on discriminatory grounds.

title: Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt by dangerous weapons or means
old_text: IPC Section 324 punished causing hurt by dangerous weapons with imprisonment up to 3 years or fine or both; IPC Section 326 punished causing grievous hurt by dangerous weapons with imprisonment for life or up to 10 years and fine.
new_text: Sub-section (1): Whoever voluntarily causes hurt by any instrument for shooting, stabbing, cutting, fire, heated substance, poison, corrosive substance, explosive, or by means of an animal, shall be punished with imprisonment up to three years, or with fine, or with both. Sub-section (2): Whoever voluntarily causes grievous hurt by any such means shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment up to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
punishment_old: Hurt with weapon (IPC 324): up to 3 years or fine or both; Grievous hurt with weapon (IPC 326): life or up to 10 years and fine.
punishment_new: Hurt with weapon (118(1)): imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both; Grievous hurt with weapon (118(2)): imprisonment for life, or up to 10 years and fine.
explanation: Consolidates causing simple hurt (IPC 324) and grievous hurt (IPC 326) with dangerous weapons into a unified two-subsection section, preserving the statutory weapons categories.

title: Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt to extort property, or to constrain to an illegal act
old_text: IPC Section 327 punished hurt for extortion with up to 10 years and fine; IPC Section 329 punished grievous hurt for extortion with life or up to 10 years and fine.
new_text: Sub-section (1): Whoever voluntarily causes hurt for the purpose of extorting property or valuable security or constraining to do an illegal act, shall be punished with imprisonment up to ten years, and fine. Sub-section (2): Whoever voluntarily causes grievous hurt for any such purpose shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment up to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
punishment_old: Hurt for extortion (IPC 327): up to 10 years and fine; Grievous hurt for extortion (IPC 329): life or up to 10 years and fine.
punishment_new: Hurt for extortion (119(1)): imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine; Grievous hurt for extortion (119(2)): imprisonment for life, or up to 10 years and fine.
explanation: Merges IPC Sections 327 and 329 into a single section with subsections differentiating simple hurt from grievous hurt inflicted during extortion.

title: Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt to extort confession, or to compel restoration of property
old_text: IPC Section 330 punished hurt to extort confession with up to 7 years and fine; IPC Section 331 punished grievous hurt to extort confession with up to 10 years and fine.
new_text: Sub-section (1): Whoever voluntarily causes hurt for the purpose of extorting a confession or information leading to detection of an offence or compelling restoration of property, shall be punished with imprisonment up to seven years, and fine. Sub-section (2): Whoever voluntarily causes grievous hurt for such purpose shall be punished with imprisonment up to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
punishment_old: Hurt for confession (IPC 330): up to 7 years and fine; Grievous hurt for confession (IPC 331): up to 10 years and fine.
punishment_new: Hurt for confession (120(1)): imprisonment up to 7 years, and fine; Grievous hurt for confession (120(2)): imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine.
explanation: Merges IPC Sections 330 and 331 into a single section penalizing custodial torture or private coercion inflicted to extract confessions or compel property restitution.

title: Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt to deter public servant from his duty
old_text: IPC Section 332 punished hurt to deter public servant with up to 3 years or fine or both; IPC Section 333 punished grievous hurt to deter public servant with up to 10 years and fine.
new_text: Sub-section (1): Whoever voluntarily causes hurt to any person being a public servant in discharge of his duty, shall be punished with imprisonment up to five years, or with fine, or with both. Sub-section (2): Whoever voluntarily causes grievous hurt for such purpose shall be punished with imprisonment not less than one year but which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
punishment_old: Hurt to public servant (IPC 332): up to 3 years or fine or both; Grievous hurt (IPC 333): up to 10 years and fine.
punishment_new: Hurt to public servant (121(1)): imprisonment up to 5 years, or fine, or both; Grievous hurt (121(2)): imprisonment 1 to 10 years, and fine.
explanation: Consolidates IPC Sections 332 and 333 while increasing the maximum prison sentence for causing simple hurt to a public servant from 3 to 5 years, and establishing a 1-year minimum floor for grievous hurt.

title: Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt on provocation
old_text: IPC Section 334 punished hurt on provocation with up to 1 month or fine up to ₹500; IPC Section 335 punished grievous hurt on provocation with up to 4 years or fine up to ₹2,000.
new_text: Sub-section (1): Whoever voluntarily causes hurt on grave and sudden provocation, without intending or knowing likely to hurt any other, shall be punished with imprisonment up to one month, or with fine up to five thousand rupees, or both. Sub-section (2): Whoever voluntarily causes grievous hurt on such provocation shall be punished with imprisonment up to five years, or with fine up to ten thousand rupees, or both.
punishment_old: Hurt on provocation (IPC 334): up to 1 month or fine ₹500; Grievous hurt (IPC 335): up to 4 years or fine ₹2,000.
punishment_new: Hurt on provocation (122(1)): imprisonment up to 1 month, or fine up to ₹5,000, or both; Grievous hurt (122(2)): imprisonment up to 5 years, or fine up to ₹10,000, or both.
explanation: Combines IPC Sections 334 and 335 into a unified mitigation section, adjusting the upper prison term for provoked grievous hurt from 4 to 5 years and significantly raising fine caps.

title: Causing hurt by means of poison, etc., with intent to commit an offence
old_text: Whoever administers to or causes to be taken by any person any poison or any stupefying, intoxicating or unwholesome drug, with intent to cause hurt or facilitate an offence, shall be punished with imprisonment up to ten years and fine.
new_text: Whoever administers to or causes to be taken by any person any poison or any stupefying, intoxicating or unwholesome drug, or other thing with intent to cause hurt to such person, or with intent to commit or to facilitate the commission of an offence, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
punishment_old: Imprisonment of either description up to 10 years, and fine.
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to 10 years, and fine.
explanation: Penalizes spiking drinks, administering date-rape drugs, poisons, or intoxicating substances to incapacitate victims or execute collateral crimes. Renumbered from IPC Section 328.

title: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt by use of acid, etc.
old_text: IPC Section 326A punished causing grievous hurt by acid with not less than 10 years up to life and fine; IPC Section 326B punished throwing or attempting to throw acid with 5 to 7 years and fine.
new_text: Sub-section (1): Whoever causes permanent or partial damage or deformity to, or burns or maims or disfigures or disables, any part of the body of a person by throwing acid, shall be punished with imprisonment not less than ten years up to imprisonment for life, and fine payable to the victim to meet medical expenses. Sub-section (2): Whoever throws or attempts to throw acid with the intention of causing damage shall be punished with imprisonment not less than five years up to seven years, and fine.
punishment_old: Acid attack (IPC 326A): min 10 years up to life and fine; Attempt to throw acid (IPC 326B): min 5 years up to 7 years and fine.
punishment_new: Acid attack (124(1)): rigorous imprisonment not less than 10 years up to life, and fine payable to victim; Attempt (124(2)): imprisonment 5 to 7 years, and fine.
explanation: Merges IPC Sections 326A and 326B into a single comprehensive acid attack statute with two subsections for consummated attacks and attempts, explicitly directing fine proceeds toward victim medical rehabilitation.

title: Act endangering life or personal safety of others
old_text: IPC Section 336 punished rash/negligent acts endangering life with up to 3 months or fine up to ₹250; IPC Section 337 punished causing hurt thereby with up to 6 months or fine up to ₹500; IPC Section 338 punished causing grievous hurt thereby with up to 2 years or fine up to ₹1,000.
new_text: Clause (a): Whoever does any act so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life or the personal safety of others, shall be punished with imprisonment up to three months, or fine up to ₹2,500, or both; Clause (b): If hurt is caused, with imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to ₹5,000, or both; Clause (c): If grievous hurt is caused, with imprisonment up to three years, or fine up to ₹10,000, or both.
punishment_old: IPC 336: up to 3 months or fine ₹250; IPC 337: up to 6 months or fine ₹500; IPC 338: up to 2 years or fine ₹1,000.
punishment_new: Endangerment (125(a)): up to 3 months or fine ₹2,500; Hurt caused (125(b)): up to 6 months or fine ₹5,000; Grievous hurt caused (125(c)): up to 3 years or fine ₹10,000, or both.
explanation: Consolidates three sequential IPC sections (336, 337, and 338) into a single streamlined section with graduated tiers, raising the maximum prison term for resulting grievous hurt from 2 to 3 years and increasing fines up to tenfold.

title: Wrongful restraint
old_text: IPC Section 339 defined wrongful restraint as voluntarily obstructing any person so as to prevent proceeding in any direction in which that person has a right to proceed; IPC Section 341 punished it with simple imprisonment up to 1 month or fine up to ₹500, or both.
new_text: Sub-section (1) defines wrongful restraint (voluntarily obstructing a person from proceeding in any direction they have a legal right to proceed, with bona fide private land obstruction excepted); Sub-section (2) punishes wrongful restraint with simple imprisonment up to one month, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both.
punishment_old: Simple imprisonment up to 1 month, or fine up to ₹500, or both (IPC 341).
punishment_new: Simple imprisonment up to 1 month, or fine up to ₹5,000, or both (BNS 126(2)).
explanation: Merges definition and penal clauses while multiplying the maximum fine tenfold from ₹500 to ₹5,000. Preserves the exception for bona fide obstruction of private pathways.

title: Wrongful confinement
old_text: IPC Section 340 defined wrongful confinement; separate sections 342-348 provided punishments for basic confinement (up to 1 year), confinement for 3+ days (up to 2 years), 10+ days (up to 3 years), in secret, for extortion, or to extort confession.
new_text: Consolidates wrongful confinement (total restraint within circumscribing boundaries) into a unified section: Sub-section (1) definition; Sub-section (2) basic confinement punished up to one year or fine up to ₹5,000 or both; Sub-section (3) confinement for 3 or more days punished up to two years or fine up to ₹10,000; Sub-section (4) confinement for 10 or more days punished up to three years and fine; Sub-sections (5)-(8) aggravated confinement in secret or for extortion/confession punished up to three to eight years.
punishment_old: Dispersed across IPC sections 342-348 ranging from 1 year to 3 years imprisonment.
punishment_new: Basic: up to 1 year or fine ₹5,000; 3+ days: up to 2 years or fine ₹10,000; 10+ days: up to 3 years and fine; Aggravated/extortion: up to 8 years and fine.
explanation: A massive structural consolidation replacing eight fragmented IPC sections (340 to 348) with a single comprehensive section governing total wrongful confinement and its duration-based and extortion-based aggravations.

title: Force
old_text: A person is said to use force to another if he causes motion, change of motion, or cessation of motion to that other, or if he causes anything to come into contact with any part of that other's body or clothes by bodily power, disposing any substance, or inducing an animal.
new_text: A person is said to use force to another if he causes motion, change of motion, or cessation of motion to that other, or if he causes to any substance such motion, change of motion, or cessation of motion as brings it into contact with any part of that other's body, or with anything which that other is wearing or carrying, by bodily power, disposing substance, or animal.
punishment_old: Substantive physical definition clause.
punishment_new: Substantive physical definition clause.
explanation: Defines the physical act of applying force under the criminal law, including motion, change of motion, or cessation of motion. Renumbered from IPC Section 349.

title: Criminal force
old_text: Whoever intentionally uses force to any person, without that person's consent, in order to the committing of any offence, or intending by the use of such force to cause, or knowing it to be likely that by the use of such force he will cause injury, fear or annoyance to the person to whom the force is used, is said to use criminal force.
new_text: Whoever intentionally uses force to any person, without that person's consent, in order to the committing of any offence, or intending by the use of such force to cause, or knowing it to be likely that by the use of such force he will cause injury, fear or annoyance to the person to whom the force is used, is said to use criminal force to that other.
punishment_old: Substantive definition; punishment prescribed under IPC Section 352.
punishment_new: Substantive definition; punishment prescribed under BNS Section 131.
explanation: Defines the penal concept of criminal force as intentional unconsented force deployed to commit an offence or cause injury, fear, or annoyance. Renumbered from IPC Section 350.

title: Assault
old_text: Whoever makes any gesture, or any preparation intending or knowing it to be likely that such gesture or preparation will cause any person present to apprehend that he who makes that gesture or preparation is about to use criminal force to that person, is said to commit an assault.
new_text: Whoever makes any gesture, or any preparation intending or knowing it to be likely that such gesture or preparation will cause any person present to apprehend that he who makes that gesture or preparation is about to use criminal force to that person, is said to commit an assault.
punishment_old: Substantive definition; punishment prescribed under IPC Section 352.
punishment_new: Substantive definition; punishment prescribed under BNS Section 131.
explanation: Defines assault as gestures or overt preparations inducing a reasonable apprehension of imminent criminal force. Clarifies that mere words do not constitute assault unless accompanied by menacing gestures. Renumbered from IPC Section 351.

title: Punishment for assault or criminal force otherwise than on grave provocation
old_text: Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any person otherwise than on grave and sudden provocation given by that person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both.
new_text: Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any person otherwise than on grave and sudden provocation given by that person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 3 months, or fine up to ₹500, or both.
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 3 months, or fine up to ₹1,000, or both.
explanation: The baseline penal clause for unprovoked assault and criminal force, doubling the maximum fine from ₹500 to ₹1,000. Renumbered from IPC Section 352.

title: Assault or criminal force to deter public servant from discharge of his duty
old_text: Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any person being a public servant in the execution of his duty as such public servant, or with intent to prevent or deter that person from discharging his duty, shall be punished with imprisonment up to two years, or with fine, or with both.
new_text: Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any person being a public servant in the execution of his duty as such public servant, or with intent to prevent or deter that person from discharging his duty as such public servant, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment of either description up to 2 years, or with fine, or with both.
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to 2 years, or with fine, or with both.
explanation: Protects public servants against physical intimidation or obstruction during execution of their lawful duties. Renumbered from IPC Section 353.

title: Assault or criminal force with intent to dishonour person, otherwise than on grave provocation
old_text: Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any person, intending thereby to dishonour that person, otherwise than on grave and sudden provocation given by that person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
new_text: Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any person, intending thereby to dishonour that person, otherwise than on grave and sudden provocation given by that person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment of either description up to 2 years, or with fine, or with both.
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to 2 years, or with fine, or with both.
explanation: Punishes acts like spitting, shoe-garlanding, or slapping intended specifically to humiliate and dishonour a person in public. Renumbered from IPC Section 355.

title: Assault or criminal force in attempt to commit theft of property carried by a person
old_text: Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any person, in attempting to commit theft on any property which that person is then wearing or carrying, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
new_text: Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any person, in attempting to commit theft on any property which that person is then wearing or carrying, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment of either description up to 2 years, or with fine, or with both.
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to 2 years, or with fine, or with both.
explanation: Penalizes physical assault committed during attempted purse-snatching, chain-snatching, or bag theft. Renumbered from IPC Section 356.

title: Assault or criminal force in attempt wrongfully to confine a person
old_text: Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any person, in attempting wrongfully to confine that person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
new_text: Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any person, in attempting wrongfully to confine that person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine up to ₹1,000, or both.
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine up to ₹5,000, or both.
explanation: Penalizes deploying physical force while attempting to corner or trap a person into wrongful confinement, raising the maximum fine from ₹1,000 to ₹5,000. Renumbered from IPC Section 357.

title: Assault or criminal force on grave provocation
old_text: Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any person on grave and sudden provocation given by that person, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to two hundred rupees, or with both.
new_text: Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any person on grave and sudden provocation given by that person, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
punishment_old: Simple imprisonment up to 1 month, or fine up to ₹200, or both.
punishment_new: Simple imprisonment up to 1 month, or fine up to ₹1,000, or both.
explanation: Mitigates punishment where assault is triggered by sudden provocation without premeditation, increasing the maximum fine from ₹200 to ₹1,000. Renumbered from IPC Section 358.

title: Kidnapping
old_text: IPC Section 359 established two types of kidnapping; Section 360 defined kidnapping from India; Section 361 defined kidnapping from lawful guardianship (under 16 for male, under 18 for female); Section 363 punished kidnapping with imprisonment up to 7 years and fine.
new_text: Consolidates the entire statutory law on kidnapping into one unified section: Sub-section (1) establishes two kinds of kidnapping (kidnapping from India and kidnapping from lawful guardianship of any child or person of unsound mind); Sub-section (2) punishes kidnapping of any person from India or from lawful guardianship with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
punishment_old: Imprisonment of either description up to 7 years, and fine (IPC Section 363).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to 7 years, and fine (BNS Section 137(2)).
explanation: Unifies the definition of kidnapping from India (IPC 360), kidnapping from lawful guardianship (IPC 361), and punishment (IPC 363) into a single cohesive section, replacing former gendered age thresholds with uniform child protection under eighteen years.

title: Abduction
old_text: Whoever by force compels, or by any deceitful means induces, any person to go from any place, is said to abduct that person.
new_text: Whoever by force compels, or by any deceitful means induces, any person to go from any place, is said to abduct that person.
punishment_old: Substantive auxiliary definition; punished under aggravated sections (IPC 364-367).
punishment_new: Substantive auxiliary definition; punished under aggravated sections (BNS 140).
explanation: Defines abduction as compelling by force or inducing by deceit any person to move from any place. Unlike kidnapping, abduction is not an offence per se unless accompanied by an unlawful intent. Renumbered from IPC Section 362.

title: Kidnapping or maiming a child for purposes of begging
old_text: Whoever kidnaps any minor or obtains custody of a minor for begging was punished with imprisonment up to 10 years and fine; whoever maimed any minor for begging was punished with imprisonment for life and fine.
new_text: Sub-section (1): Whoever kidnaps any child or not being the lawful guardian obtains custody of a child, in order that such child may be employed or used for the purpose of begging, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment not less than seven years but which may extend to ten years, and fine. Sub-section (2): Whoever maims any child in order that such child may be employed or used for begging, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for life (remainder of natural life) and fine.
punishment_old: Kidnapping for begging: up to 10 years and fine; Maiming for begging: imprisonment for life and fine (IPC 363A).
punishment_new: Kidnapping for begging (139(1)): rigorous imprisonment not less than 7 years up to 10 years, and fine; Maiming for begging (139(2)): rigorous imprisonment for remainder of natural life, and fine.
explanation: Significantly strengthens protections against begging cartels by establishing a mandatory minimum sentence of 7 years for kidnapping a child for begging, and upgrading the penalty for maiming a child to imprisonment for the remainder of natural life.

title: Kidnapping or abducting in order to murder or for ransom, etc.
old_text: IPC Section 364 punished kidnapping to murder with life or up to 10 years; Section 364A punished kidnapping for ransom with death or life imprisonment; Section 365 punished secret confinement with up to 7 years; Section 367 punished kidnapping to subject to grievous hurt with up to 10 years.
new_text: Sub-section (1): Whoever kidnaps or abducts any person in order that such person may be murdered or subjected to danger of being murdered, shall be punished with imprisonment for life or rigorous imprisonment up to ten years, and fine; Sub-section (2): Whoever kidnaps or abducts any person and threatens to cause death or hurt to compel government or person to pay ransom or do an act, shall be punished with death or imprisonment for life, and fine; Sub-section (3): Kidnapping to secretly confine punished up to seven years and fine.
punishment_old: Murder (IPC 364): life or 10 yrs; Ransom (IPC 364A): death or life; Secret confinement (IPC 365): 7 yrs.
punishment_new: In order to murder (140(1)): life or rigorous imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine; For ransom/compulsion (140(2)): death or imprisonment for life, and fine; Secret confinement (140(3)): imprisonment up to 7 years and fine.
explanation: Consolidates all aggravated kidnapping and abduction crimes (for murder, ransom, and secret detention) into a structured section with distinct sub-clauses, preserving capital punishment for kidnapping for ransom.

title: Importation of girl or boy from foreign country
old_text: Whoever imports into India from any country outside India any girl under the age of twenty-one years with intent that she may be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse, shall be punishable with imprisonment up to ten years and fine (IPC Section 366B applied only to girls).
new_text: Whoever imports into India from any country outside India or from the State of Jammu and Kashmir any girl or boy under the age of eighteen years with intent that such person may be, or knowing it to be likely that such person will be, forced or seduced to illicit intercourse, shall be punishable with imprisonment which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 10 years and fine (applicable only to girls under 21).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to 10 years, and fine (gender-neutral: any girl or boy under 18).
explanation: Transforms the cross-border sex trafficking provision to be fully gender-neutral by explicitly including boys, while standardizing the age threshold to under eighteen years. Modified from IPC Section 366B.

title: Wrongfully concealing or keeping in confinement, kidnapped or abducted person
old_text: Whoever, knowing that any person has been kidnapped or has been abducted, wrongfully conceals or confines such person, shall be punished in the same manner as if he had kidnapped or abducted such person.
new_text: Whoever, knowing that any person has been kidnapped or has been abducted, wrongfully conceals or confines such person, shall be punished in the same manner as if he had kidnapped or abducted such person with the same intention or knowledge, or for the same purpose.
punishment_old: Punished as if the concealer had directly executed the kidnapping or abduction.
punishment_new: Punished as if the concealer had directly executed the kidnapping or abduction.
explanation: Extends principal criminal liability to safehouse keepers and conspirators who conceal or harbour kidnapped victims after the abduction. Renumbered from IPC Section 368.

title: Trafficking of person
old_text: Whoever, for the purpose of exploitation, recruits, transports, harbours, transfers, or receives a person by using threats, force, abduction, fraud, or abuse of power, commits trafficking, punished with rigorous imprisonment 7 to 10 years; trafficking of minor: 10 to 14 years; trafficking of multiple persons: 14 years to life.
new_text: Whoever recruits, transports, harbours, transfers, or receives a person for exploitation by threats, force, abduction, fraud, deception, or abuse of power commits trafficking: Sub-section (2) single person punished with rigorous imprisonment 7 to 10 years and fine; Sub-section (3) more than one person punished with rigorous imprisonment 10 years to life and fine; Sub-section (4) trafficking of child punished with rigorous imprisonment not less than ten years up to life, and fine; Sub-section (5) trafficking of child on more than one occasion punished with imprisonment for remainder of natural life or death.
punishment_old: Single person: 7 to 10 years; Minor: 10 to 14 years; Multiple minors: 14 years to life (IPC 370).
punishment_new: Single person: 7 to 10 years; Multiple persons: 10 years to life; Child trafficking: min 10 years up to life; Repeat child trafficking: remainder of natural life or death (BNS 143(5)).
explanation: Comprehensive anti-human trafficking statute with significantly escalated sentencing. Crucially, Section 143(5) introduces life imprisonment for natural life or capital punishment for syndicates or individuals trafficking children on multiple occasions.

title: Exploitation of a trafficked person
old_text: Whoever, knowingly or having reason to believe that a person has been trafficked, exploits such person in any manner shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment not less than 5 years up to 7 years (for adult) or 7 years up to 10 years (for minor).
new_text: Sub-section (1): Whoever, knowingly or having reason to believe that a child has been trafficked, exploits such child in any manner shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than seven years but which may extend to ten years, and fine. Sub-section (2): Whoever exploits an adult trafficked person shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment not less than five years but which may extend to seven years, and fine.
punishment_old: Trafficked child: 7 to 10 years and fine; Trafficked adult: 5 to 7 years and fine (IPC Section 370A).
punishment_new: Trafficked child (144(1)): rigorous imprisonment 7 to 10 years and fine; Trafficked adult (144(2)): rigorous imprisonment 5 to 7 years and fine.
explanation: Penalizes clients, employers, and beneficiaries who exploit persons knowing they have been trafficked, maintaining higher minimum sentences when children are exploited. Renumbered from IPC Section 370A.

title: Habitual dealing in slaves
old_text: Whoever habitually imports, exports, removes, buys, sells, traffics or deals in slaves, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
new_text: Whoever habitually imports, exports, removes, buys, sells, traffics or deals in slaves, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
punishment_old: Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine.
punishment_new: Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine.
explanation: Criminalizes habitual involvement in the slave trade, slave trafficking, or dealing in human chattel. Renumbered from IPC Section 371.

title: Unlawful compulsory labour
old_text: Whoever unlawfully compulsorily compels any person to labour against the will of that person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.
new_text: Whoever unlawfully compels any person to labour against the will of that person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment of either description up to 1 year, or with fine, or with both.
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to 1 year, or with fine, or with both.
explanation: Penalizes forced labour, begar, and involuntary compulsory service in furtherance of Article 23 constitutional guarantees. Marks the concluding section of Chapter VI. Renumbered from IPC Section 374.
